title: A delegated coding session leaves no record this loop can read
summary: delegate_fix runs a whole coding session and the only thing it leaves behind is the A2A task JSON, which records the request, the state and the git artifact -- not a trace. records.py looks for run.json, trace.json or trace.jsonl, so a delegated session is invisible to the corpus the improvement loop reads.
diagnosis:
peers._register_code calls agent.code.a2a.make_handler without a trace_path, so run_session writes no run tree for the delegate. The flat EVAL_TRACE_FILE trace does capture the delegate's calls -- it is inherited through the run config -- but it lands in the caller's file, so the delegation cannot be read back as a run of its own.

The consequence is exactly the gap the first pass fell into: the only account of what a delegation did is the delegate's own closing message, which is the one source this project already knows not to trust.
fix: Pass a trace_path into make_handler from peers._register_code, under the caller's record directory, so a delegated session writes its own run tree beside the task JSON. Needs LANGSMITH_TRACING to produce anything, so state that limitation rather than assuming it.

history.detail: Filed by hand from the first live improvement pass, 2026-09-08.

Reopened by review. This closed on considered>0, matched=0 while its signature had never matched a run -- there was no baseline to have moved away from, so nothing was learned. The rule that now returns `unproven` instead landed after this closure. The problem is unverified, not gone; the signature is the part that needs work.
